Exampleshire Borough Council (202312345)

Published 3 July 2024

REPORT

COMPLAINT 202312345

Exampleshire Borough Council

17 June 2024

Our approach

This is invented boilerplate for a test fixture. It describes, in made-up words, how a fictional reviewer reads a complaint.

A second invented boilerplate paragraph, which carries no paragraph number.

The complaint

1. The complaint concerns the council’s response to the tenant’s reports of damp and mould in the back bedroom.

2. We have also looked at how the council dealt with the complaint itself.

Background

3. The tenant rents a two-bedroom flat from the council on a secure tenancy.

4. The tenant first reported black mould on the bedroom wall in March 2023.

5. An operative visited and wiped the wall but did not look for the cause.

Assessment and findings

Scope of investigation

6. This report covers events from March 2023 to the council’s final response.

The landlord’s handling of the reports of damp and mould

7. The council was slow to inspect. The tenant wrote to it as follows:

“Our clothes all smell of the damp wall.”

8. The council kept no record of its visits.

Complaint handling

9. The council answered the complaint late.

Determination

10. In accordance with paragraph 52 of the Scheme, there was maladministration in the council’s handling of the tenant’s reports of damp and mould.

11. In accordance with paragraph 52 of the Scheme, there was service failure in the council’s complaint handling.

Orders and recommendations

Orders

12. Within 4 weeks of this report the council must pay the tenant:

(a) £500 for the distress caused by its handling of the damp and mould;

(b) £150 for its complaint handling.

13. The council must inspect the flat and send the tenant a schedule of works.
(a) A qualified surveyor must carry out the inspection.
(b) The schedule must give target dates.
